title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Caltex staff
tiers.description: Directors, full-time, part-time and casual employees, consultants, secondees, contractors of, and persons seconded to, the Caltex Group. Staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade at any time provided they hold no inside information; none of the closed periods, clearance requirements or trading restrictions (derivatives, short-term, short selling, hedging, margin lending and secured financing) apply to them.

tiers.name: Designated Caltex Personnel
tiers.description: Caltex Australia Limited Directors (including alternate Directors), Caltex Australia Limited Leadership Team (CLT) members, and Caltex staff who have been notified that they are Designated Caltex Personnel. This tier carries the closed periods, the trading clearance regime, the post-trade notification duty and all of the substantive trading restrictions. The only differentiation within the tier is the identity of the clearance approver.

tiers.name: closely connected persons
tiers.description: Immediate family members, companies and businesses in which Caltex staff hold a controlling interest and/or are a Director or Trustee where Caltex staff are beneficiaries. Designated Caltex Personnel must take reasonable steps, including notifying them of closed periods, to prevent them trading in any way prohibited by the policy.

definitions.hedging_definition: any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities, including vested Caltex securities or unvested entitlements to Caltex securities under Caltex employee incentive schemes

windows.end_anchor: the day after Caltex's half year results are released to ASX
the day after Caltex's full year results are released to ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Caltex Board may designate any other period as a black-out period; it must be advised to the Designated Caltex Personnel, so it is notified to those affected but not necessarily announced to the market. Separately, clearance may be withheld for perception reasons without reasons being given, and a refusal must be kept confidential by the applicant.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Trading in Derivatives; Definitions
rules.detail: The policy expressly extends to derivative markets and derivative products, naming warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences, over both vested securities and unvested entitlements, and Caltex securities are defined to include third-party issued options and swaps. A derivative is therefore a trade requiring clearance, outside closed periods, with post-trade notification. This does not rescue collar legs: any derivative that limits risk exposure is separately prohibited by the hedging ban.
rules.evidence: This policy applies to transactions in derivative markets and trading involving derivative products (including warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences) issued over or in respect of vested Caltex securities and unvested entitlements to Caltex securities.

rules.detail: Staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel are outside the closed periods, the clearance regime and the Trading Restrictions section, so a derivative over Caltex securities is limited only by the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.

rules.detail: An effects-based ban on any arrangement limiting risk exposure to Caltex securities, expressly extended to vested securities. There is no approval route, no de minimis and no venue limit; the exceptional circumstances discretion relieves only against the closed period prohibition, not against this restriction.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities, including vested Caltex securities or unvested entitlements to Caltex securities under Caltex employee incentive schemes.

rules.detail: The same ban expressly reaches unvested entitlements under Caltex employee incentive schemes, so unvested rights cannot be hedged or used as the reference asset for a derivative.
rules.evidence: including vested Caltex securities or unvested entitlements to Caltex securities under Caltex employee incentive schemes.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Hedging Transactions; Insider Trading Prohibition
rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is expressed to bind Designated Caltex Personnel only, so staff outside that tier are not prohibited from hedging; the insider trading prohibition still applies at all times.
rules.evidence: Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Hedging Transactions; Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collar-plus-loan structures are not named. Each has the effect of limiting risk exposure to Caltex securities and so falls within the hedging ban, and if the advance is secured on the shares it is separately caught by the secured financing prohibition.
rules.evidence: prohibited from entering into any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities

rules.detail: Flat ban on entering into any arrangements for short selling Caltex securities, with no approval route or security-state carve-out. The reference to 'any arrangements' would reach synthetic short exposure as well as physical short sales.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any arrangements for short selling Caltex securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named. A stock loan transfers the legal interest in the security and is therefore a 'trade', so it would need clearance, fall outside closed periods and be notified within three days; it is not separately prohibited unless it forms part of a short selling or risk-limiting arrangement.
rules.evidence: "trade" includes subscribing for, buying, selling or otherwise transferring the beneficial or legal interest in a security.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Trading in Derivatives, Short-term Trading, Short Selling, Hedging Transactions
rules.detail: Contracts for differences are expressly brought within the policy, so they are trades requiring clearance rather than being outside it. In practice most CFD positions are separately prohibited: a short CFD by the short selling ban, a risk-limiting CFD by the hedging ban, and any CFD closed out within six months by the short-term trading ban.
rules.evidence: This policy applies to transactions in derivative markets and trading involving derivative products (including warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences)

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
rules.detail: Margin lending in respect of Caltex securities is expressly prohibited at all times for all Designated Caltex Personnel, with no approval route, no vesting carve-out and no grandfathering.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
rules.detail: Granting security over Caltex securities to support financing is prohibited as a secured financing arrangement. A charge, lien or pledge unconnected with any financing is not named, and the definition of 'trade' does not expressly sweep in the creation of a security interest.
rules.evidence: prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
rules.detail: The prohibition is deliberately wider than margin loans, extending to 'other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities'. It binds every Director and CLT member regardless of security state, has no clearance or waiver route, and the exceptional circumstances discretion is confined to closed period trading.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.

rules.detail: Six month ban on short-term or speculative trading, expressly extended to derivative products issued over or in respect of Caltex securities, with purchase and sale of the same securities within six months given as an inclusive example. No stated matching basis and no carve-out for plan securities.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from engaging in short term or speculative trading in Caltex securities or derivative products issued over or in respect of Caltex securities, including purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities within a six month period.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary for all Designated Caltex Personnel except Directors; Chairman of the Board for Directors (excluding the Chairman); Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board. Requests go by email to secretariat@caltex.com.au and the Company Secretary follows an Internal Approval Process before confirming.
clearance.post_trade_to: Caltex Secretariat (contract note, or an email with holder name, SRN/HIN, number or dollar value, price, date and nature of trade); Directors should also notify the Company Secretary as soon as practical after any Permitted Trading
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no later than three days after the date of the trade
clearance.evidence: Clearance for trading in Caltex securities is only valid for trading notified in the request for clearance and will lapse 14 calendar days after the date the clearance was granted. ... The Caltex Secretariat will respond to requests for clearance to trade in Caltex securities within one business day of receipt of the request.
Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.

clearance.section: Trading Restrictions - Trading by Connected Persons
clearance.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel must take reasonable steps, including notifying their closely connected persons of closed periods, to prevent any closely connected persons from trading in Caltex securities in any way that is prohibited under this policy.

short_term.basis: purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities, given as an inclusive example of short term or speculative trading; expressly extends to derivative products over Caltex securities
short_term.evidence: including purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities within a six month period.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the Board for Directors and CLT; Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship if, in the opinion of the person exercising the discretion, they are only able to meet their financial commitments by selling their securities ... and the proposed disposal of Caltex securities is the only reasonable course of action to overcome these circumstances.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the Board for Directors and CLT; Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board
exceptions.evidence: to give effect to a court order, court enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the Board for Directors and CLT; Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board

exceptions.evidence: acquisition of securities under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders in Caltex, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan or an equal access buy-back, where the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Caltex Board;
disposal of securities arising from the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme or arrangement or equal access buy-back;
transfers of Caltex securities where there is no change in the person's underlying beneficial interest in the securities;
transfers of securities between someone closely related such as a spouse, minor child, family company or family trust or to their superannuation fund;

disposal by Designated Caltex Personnel of Caltex securities under a pre-determined divestment plan where the plan cannot be cancelled during a closed period (other than in exceptional circumstances) and: they entered into the plan outside a closed period; they have not amended the plan during a closed period; the plan does not permit them to exercise any discretion over how, when and whether to dispose of securities.

indirect or incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of Designated Caltex Personnel dealing in securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold as part of its portfolio securities in Caltex;

The restrictions on trading during closed periods do not apply to: offers made to Caltex staff to participate in Caltex short and long term incentive plans and share plans (together, Plans); acceptance by Caltex staff of offers referred to above ... and transfers of unrestricted Caltex securities from the Trustee of any of the Plans to Caltex staff

external_documents: Internal Approval Process followed by the Company Secretary before confirming clearance to trade
exemption_authority: The Chairman of the Board (for Directors and CLT) and the Chairman of the Audit Committee (for the Chairman of the Board) have a discretion to exempt from the closed period prohibition only, and only for severe financial hardship, exceptional personal circumstances, or to give effect to a court order, court enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement, where disposal is the only reasonable course of action. No person has authority to waive the hedging, short selling, short-term trading, margin lending or secured financing prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.topic: effects-based hedging ban over vested shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities, including vested Caltex securities or unvested entitlements to Caltex securities under Caltex employee incentive schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is drafted by economic effect and expressly reaches vested shares, so the purchased put and written call of a collar are prohibited outright for every Director and CLT member with no approval or hardship route.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured financing wider than margin lending
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is independently prohibited, so the funded element fails even before the hedging ban is considered.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to transactions in derivative markets and trading involving derivative products (including warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences) issued over or in respect of vested Caltex securities and unvested entitlements to Caltex securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no argument that a bilateral OTC collar sits outside the policy; it is expressly captured, over both vested and unvested exposure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "Caltex securities" includes ordinary shares of Caltex and any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, option, warrant, or other derivative over an ordinary share of Caltex, whether issued by Caltex or a third party, and any other interest in an ordinary share of Caltex.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank-written put and call are themselves Caltex securities, so the six month short-term trading ban and the closed period restrictions apply to the derivative legs and to any roll or unwind, not just to the underlying shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: six month short-term ban including derivatives
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from engaging in short term or speculative trading in Caltex securities or derivative products issued over or in respect of Caltex securities, including purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities within a six month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if hedging were permitted, any collar with a tenor, roll or early unwind inside six months would be separately prohibited as short-term or speculative trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance ... will lapse 14 calendar days after the date the clearance was granted ... Clearance to trade can be given or refused without giving any reasons and may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. If clearance to trade is refused, the person seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted transaction must be executed inside 14 calendar days, can be revoked between grant and execution, and the executive cannot tell the bank why a refusal occurred.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any clearance to trade may be withheld for perception reasons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant transaction can be blocked on reputational grounds alone, which is precisely the ground on which a director's collar would be scrutinised.

bespoke_clauses.topic: transfer to a third party holding is a trade
bespoke_clauses.clause: Nature of proposed trade (i.e. on market purchase, on-market transfer or sale, transfer to super fund).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The clearance form treats a transfer to another holding vehicle as a notifiable trade, so moving collared shares into a bank custody or security account would require clearance and post-trade notification, even though transfers with no change in beneficial interest are listed as Permitted Trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Caltex Personnel must notify the Caltex Secretariat of details of any trading in Caltex securities by submitting a contract note to secretariat@caltex.com.au no later than three days after the date of the trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any collar entry, roll or unwind by a Director or CLT member is reported to the Secretariat within three days and, for Directors, flows into ASX disclosure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "closely connected persons" of Caltex staff include immediate family members, companies and businesses in which Caltex staff hold a controlling interest and/or are a Director or Trustee where Caltex staff are beneficiaries.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares through a family company or trust does not escape the hedging and secured financing prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: All of the collar-relevant prohibitions bind only Designated Caltex Personnel, but any employee can be notified into that tier at any time, so a counterparty cannot rely on a client remaining outside it for the life of the trade.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for any Ampol (Caltex) Director or Leadership Team member. Both legs of the structure are separately and expressly prohibited: the hedging restriction bans 'any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities, including vested Caltex securities', and the financing restriction bans 'any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities'. Neither prohibition has an approval route, and the only discretion in the policy, exercisable by the Chairman of the Board or the Chairman of the Audit Committee, relieves solely against the closed period restriction on grounds of severe hardship, exceptional personal circumstances or a court order. The policy expressly captures over-the-counter options and contracts for differences, and defines third-party derivatives over Caltex shares as Caltex securities, so no cash-settled or offshore variant escapes it, and the six month short-term trading ban would independently bar a short-dated collar. Only Caltex staff outside the Designated Caltex Personnel tier fall outside these restrictions, and any employee can be notified into that tier at any time.
